+- [Execution Modes & Workflows](#execution-modes--workflows)
+  - [Interactive TUI](#interactive-terminal-ui)
+  - [Command-Line REPL](#command-line-repl)
+  - [Autonomous Non-Interactive Run](#autonomous-task-execution)
+- [Core Capabilities](#core-capabilities)
+  - [Security & Sandboxing](#-defense-in-depth-sandboxing)
+  - [Git Worktree Isolation](#-git-worktree-isolation)
+  - [Human-in-the-Loop Controls](#-human-in-the-loop-hitl-approvals)
+  - [Context Budgeting & Cost Governance](#-context-budgeting--cost-governance)
+  - [Universal Model Ecosystem & MCP](#-universal-model-support--mcp)
+- [Common Commands & Slash Actions](#common-commands--slash-actions)
+- [Building from Source](#building-from-source)
+- [Repository Structure](#repository-structure)
+- [Documentation Index](#documentation-index)
+- [Contributing & Community](#contributing--community)
+- [License](#license)
 
-The unversioned installer follows the latest stable release. If no stable release has been published yet, it exits with a hint to select a prerelease tag. To install a prerelease or pin a version, use the tag shown on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/releases) and set `NEXUS_VERSION`; see the [quickstart](quickstart.md).
+---
+
+## Why Nexus Code?
+
+Most agentic coding tools operate either as black-box cloud subscriptions or as unconstrained local scripts with unrestricted shell access. Nexus Code takes a systems-engineering approach:
+
+- **Security by Default:** All agent actions (filesystem writes, command executions, child processes) run within unprivileged Linux Bubblewrap (`bwrap`) sandboxes and strict kernel resource limits (`prlimit`), with optional Docker container isolation.
+- **Git Worktree Isolation:** Rather than mutating your active checkout, speculative code changes and verification loops occur in dedicated, lightweight Git worktrees (`.nexus/worktrees/`), complete with verification receipts and clean fast-forward squashes.
+- **Thoughtfully Designed TUI:** Built on [Ratatui](https://ratatui.rs/), the live terminal interface delivers smooth token streaming, instant keyboard approvals, unified diff review, proportional modal overlays, and resilient paste management.
+- **Deterministic Verification:** Nexus Code refuses to guess whether code works. It establishes verifiable test baselines before modification and requires deliverable-bound verifier checks before merging.
+- **Cost & Context Protection:** Real-time token capacity tracking, automatic context compaction, and hard budget limits (`NEXUS_CLOUD_MAX_COST_USD`) prevent runaway API spending.
+
+---
+
+## Architecture Overview
+
+Nexus Code uses a hybrid, decoupled architecture:
+1. **Front-End & Terminal Experience (`core/src/bin/nexus_tui`):** High-performance Rust binary utilizing Ratatui and crossterm for zero-flicker diff rendering, event handling, and terminal management.
+2. **Agent Brain & Sidecar (`cli/`):** TypeScript-driven execution loop handling turn dispatch, LLM conversation state, tool calling, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and context compaction.
+3. **Workspace Tools Engine (`core/src/` / `harness-core`):** Rust native library implementing high-throughput file operations, unified diff generation, syntax inspection, and sandboxed command execution.
+
+```mermaid
+graph TD
+    User([Developer / Terminal]) <-->|Keystrokes / ANSI Output| TUI[nexus-tui\nRatatui / Rust]
+    TUI <-->|Bidirectional JSON-RPC / Unix Pipe| Sidecar[Agent Sidecar\nTypeScript / Node.js 22+]
+    
+    subgraph Agent Runtime
+        Sidecar --> Context[Context Budgeting & Compaction]
+        Sidecar --> Approval[Approval Policy & Egress Guard]
+        Sidecar --> Models[Local & Cloud LLMs\nvLLM / Ollama / Anthropic / OpenAI]
+        Sidecar --> MCP[Model Context Protocol Hub]
+    end
+
+    Sidecar <-->|Fast IPC / CLI| CoreTools[harness-core\nRust Native Engine]
+
+    subgraph Sandboxed Workspace
+        CoreTools --> Sandbox[Linux bwrap / prlimit / Docker]
+        Sandbox --> Worktrees[Git Worktree Isolation\nfeat/branch-name]
+        Worktrees --> Disk[(Project Workspace)]
+    end
+```
+
+---
+
+## Quick Start
+
+### 1. Installation
+
+On Linux x86-64 (glibc 2.35+ and Node.js 22+):
 
 ```sh
 curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/main/install.sh | sh
 ```
 
-This follows the latest stable release and installs the Linux x86-64 package under your home directory. The installer verifies its SHA-256 checksum and requires Node.js 22 or newer. To pin a specific version or install a prerelease, set `NEXUS_VERSION` to that release's tag. See [release status and platform requirements](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).
+The installer verifies SHA-256 checksums, installs the client package into `~/.local/lib/nexus`, and creates a symlink at `~/.local/bin/nexus`. Ensure `~/.local/bin` is in your `PATH`:
+
+```sh
+export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
+```
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> To pin a specific release version, set `NEXUS_VERSION`:
+> ```sh
+> curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/main/install.sh | NEXUS_VERSION=v1.1.4 sh
+> ```
+
+### 2. Inference Setup
+
+Nexus Code connects to any OpenAI-compatible local server (e.g. Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio) or cloud provider.
+
+Configure your endpoint in `~/.config/nexus/config.env`:
+
+```sh
+mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/nexus"
+chmod 700 "$HOME/.config/nexus"
+cat > "$HOME/.config/nexus/config.env" <<'EOF'
+LOCAL_LLM_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:1234/v1
+LOCAL_LLM_MODEL=qwen2.5-coder-7b-instruct
+LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY=REDACTED
+EOF
+chmod 600 "$HOME/.config/nexus/config.env"
+```
+
+For cloud providers (Anthropic Claude or OpenAI), see [Cloud Providers Guide](docs/CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md).
+
+### 3. First Run
+
+Navigate to any git repository and start Nexus Code:
+
+```sh
+cd /path/to/your/project
+nexus
+```
+
+---
+
+## Execution Modes & Workflows
+
+### Interactive Terminal UI
+Running `nexus` in a standard terminal launches the full-screen interactive TUI:
+```sh
+nexus
+```
+- Real-time token streaming and syntax highlighting.
+- Visual approval prompt for shell execution and file modification.
+- Multi-line composer with history search and bracketed paste handling.
+- Use `/help` for available slash commands, `/model` to switch providers, or `Esc` to cancel the active turn.
+
+### Command-Line REPL
+For terminal multiplexers, remote SSH sessions, or plain terminal workflows:
+```sh
+nexus repl
+```
+Provides the full conversational agent with line-based interactive approval prompts.
+
+### Autonomous Task Execution
+Execute a targeted objective headlessly and exit upon verified completion:
+```sh
+nexus run "Add unit tests for the token bucket rate limiter in src/rate_limiter.ts"
+```
+Nexus will explore the codebase, plan edits, execute tests inside the sandbox, verify outcomes against your deliverable baseline, and record an audit trail.
+
+---
+
+## Core Capabilities
+
+### 🛡️ Defense-in-Depth Sandboxing
+Every command executed by the agent runs in an isolated sandbox:
+- **Bubblewrap (`bwrap`) Isolation:** Mounts the root filesystem read-only, providing dedicated writable mounts only for the workspace.
+- **Process Resource Limits (`prlimit`):** Caps CPU time, memory consumption (AS/RSS), max open file descriptors, and total process count.
+- **Network Egress Guard:** Unauthorized network calls from within the sandbox are blocked unless explicitly permitted by policy.
+
+### 🌲 Git Worktree Isolation
+Eliminate uncommitted workspace pollution with native named worktrees (see [docs/WORKTREES.md](docs/WORKTREES.md)):
+- Run speculative features under `.nexus/worktrees/<branch>` (or configured sibling directories) with zero risk to your checked-out files.
+- Command `nexus worktree switch -c <branch>` (or session `/worktree switch -c <branch>`) creates an isolated branch checkout.
+- Fast-forward verified changes, remove completed worktrees with `nexus worktree remove <branch>`, and inspect status with `nexus worktree list --json`.
+
+### 🤝 Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Approvals
+Stay in complete control of changes:
+- **`review` mode (default):** Prompts for confirmation before executing file writes, shell invocations, or network calls.
+- **`auto` mode:** Autonomous file edits and test runs; asks for approval only on first-time egress to new network endpoints.
+- **`read-only` mode:** Strictly forbids write operations and mutative commands; safe for auditing untrusted codebases.
+
+### 🧠 Context Budgeting & Cost Governance
+- Tracks token consumption per step against discovered model context limits.
+- Automatic compaction summarizes older conversation turns when context headroom shrinks.
+- Enforces strict cloud cost ceilings via `NEXUS_CLOUD_MAX_COST_USD`.
+
+### 🔌 Universal Model Support & MCP
+- Local inference: native support for llama.cpp, Ollama, and vLLM (see [docs/LOCAL_SERVERS.md](docs/LOCAL_SERVERS.md)).
+- Cloud provider support with secret redaction and configurable cost governance (see [docs/CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md](docs/CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md)).
+- Full support for Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients and servers to expose external tools and resource context.
+
+---
+
+## Common Commands & Slash Actions
+
+| Command | Shortcut | Description |
+|---|---|---|
+| `/help` | `?` | List the slash commands and keybindings |
+| `/model` | `Ctrl+P` | Choose a model from any connected provider (Ctrl+P connects one) |
+| `/status` | — | Show workspace, model, mode, endpoint, and session info |
+| `/worktree` | — | Manage speculative and named git worktrees (`status`, `merge`, `discard`, `list`, `switch`, `remove`) |
+| `/diff` | — | Show uncommitted changes as a syntax-highlighted unified diff |
+| `/commit` | — | Commit changes; suggests a conventional commit message if omitted |
+| `/doctor` | — | Diagnose configuration, endpoint, engine, shell, and session state |
+| `/tokens` | — | Display context window use and session token totals |
+| `/receipt` | — | Show turn outcome, verifier evidence, and validation receipt |
+| `/clear` | — | Reset conversation context for a clean task turn |
+| `/exit` | `Ctrl+C` | Cleanly exit session and print session resume command |
+
+---
+
+## Building from Source
+
+### Prerequisites
+- **Linux x86-64** with glibc 2.35+
+- **Node.js** 22.0.0 or higher & `npm`
+- **Rust** 2024 edition (MSRV 1.85.0+, pinned toolchain 1.95.0 in `rust-toolchain.toml`) & `cargo`
+- **C compiler & linker** (`gcc` or `clang`), `make`, `pkg-config`
+
+### Build Steps
+
+```sh
+# 1. Clone repository
+git clone https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code.git
+cd nexus-code
+
+# 2. Install CLI dependencies
+npm ci --prefix cli
+
+# 3. Build native Rust binaries and TypeScript distribution
+make build
+
+# 4. Run test suites
+make test
+```
+
+For running comprehensive CI tests locally (including bubblewrap isolation fixtures):
+```sh
+sudo make test-ci
+```
+
+---
+
+## Repository Structure
+
+```
+nexus-code/
+├── cli/                   # TypeScript agent brain, REPL, slash router, and sidecar
+│   ├── src/               # Agent loops, sandbox adapters, tokens, and git integrations
+│   └── test/              # Integration and unit tests
+├── core/                  # Rust workspace tools and Ratatui terminal UI
+│   ├── src/bin/nexus_tui/ # Live TUI: views, diff cards, composer, markdown
+│   └── src/               # File operations, sandboxing, unified diffs, syntax
+├── docs/                  # Architecture specs, user manuals, and provider guides
+├── experiments/           # Cloudflare Workers & Artifacts collaboration slices
+├── scripts/               # Release packaging, CI runners, and security gates
+└── tasks/                 # Production roadmap, audit tracking, and issue ledgers
+```
+
+---
+
+## Documentation Index
+
+Explore our comprehensive guides in the [`docs/`](docs/) directory:
+
+- 📖 **[User Manual](docs/USER_MANUAL.md):** Complete guide to interactive workflows, approval postures, and session management.
+- 🚀 **[Quickstart Guide](quickstart.md):** Installation, configuration, and running your first task in 60 seconds.
+- 🏗️ **[Architecture Reference](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md):** Deep dive into the process model, security guarantees, and execution loop.
+- 🌲 **[Worktree Operations](docs/WORKTREES.md):** Guide to isolated branching, receipt gates, and conflict-free merges.
+- 🖥️ **[Local Servers Guide](docs/LOCAL_SERVERS.md):** Instructions for configuring Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, and llama.cpp.
+- ☁️ **[Cloud Providers Guide](docs/CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md):** Setup for Anthropic, OpenAI, custom endpoints, and secret redaction.
+- 🛠️ **[Developer & Release Guide](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md):** Contributing, local test gates, reproducible builds, and releases.
+- 🩺 **[Doctor & Troubleshooting](docs/DOCTOR_TROUBLESHOOTING.md):** Diagnosing common environment, sandbox, and provider issues.
+
+---
+
+## Contributing & Community
 
-## Build and contribute
+We welcome contributions from the community! Nexus Code is built with rigorous engineering standards:
 
-See [development and release procedures](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md), [client guide](docs/CLIENT_GUIDE.md), [provider setup](docs/CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md), and the [contest entry](docs/CLOUDFLARE_CONTEST.md).
+- **Contribution Guidelines:** Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting pull requests.

content.content:
## Commands

```
nexus worktree switch -c feature/login          # create branch + worktree from the default branch
nexus worktree switch feature/login             # print/refresh the worktree of an existing branch
nexus worktree list --json                      # dirty, ahead/behind, integrated, age (schema 1)
nexus worktree path feature/login
nexus worktree remove feature/login
nexus worktree copy-ignored --to feature/login --dry-run
nexus worktree merge                            # from inside the worktree: squash, rebase, fast-forward, clean up
nexus worktree prune --dry-run --min-age 1d
```

Shortcuts work wherever a branch is accepted: `^` the default branch, `@` the branch of the current worktree, `-` the
branch that was active before the last `switch`. A worktree path is accepted too.

`remove` refuses a worktree with changes, untracked or ignored files (`--force` overrides), a branch that is not merged
into the default branch (`--delete-unmerged` overrides), the main checkout, the worktree you are standing in, a locked
worktree and a speculative task worktree (unless `--force`).

## Running a task in a named worktree

`nexus run --worktree-branch feature/login "task"` (also on `nexus repl` and `nexus live`) runs the task inside the named worktree
for that branch, creating it from the default branch when it does not exist and reusing it when it does. It has the same
sandbox requirement as `--worktree`. The branch must not be the one checked out in the primary checkout (`--worktree-branch main`
is refused: running there would not be isolated). Unlike the ephemeral task worktree, a named worktree is never auto-merged or
discarded: when the task ends it stays, later runs and follow-up `repl`/`live` prompts in the same session continue inside it, and a
passing verifier run inside it records the verification that `nexus worktree merge` needs. After an in-session merge
of that branch removes the worktree, a later turn in a session still started with `--worktree-branch` creates the branch
again (it is created when missing). The
task state records a binding of kind `named` (binding version 1); builds that predate it ignore the kind and cannot merge or discard
it, because their paths are derived from `nexus/<task-id>`.

## Merge and prune

`merge [target]` (default: the default branch) commits uncommitted changes with a deterministic message (or `-m`), squashes
the branch to one commit (`--no-squash` keeps them), rebases onto the target (`--no-rebase` skips it), fast-forwards the
target (never a merge commit) and removes the worktree and branch (`--no-remove` keeps them). The target's worktree must be
clean. The state being merged (HEAD, plus uncommitted work) needs a recorded passing verification: a Nexus session records one
when its deliverable-bound verifier passes inside that worktree (the verifier must be the configured `--authoritative-verifier` or an independent one, never a discovered generic command), keyed by branch, head and tree, so a later edit or commit
no longer matches. Without one, merge refuses unless you pass `--no-verify-receipt --reason "why"`; the waiver (branch, head,
reason) is recorded in the registry. A session that starts in a worktree that already holds uncommitted work (or one that cannot be certified, such as one with a nested repository or a missing or replaced `.git`; judged where the session starts, so its own later verified work does not count) verifies as usual, but its baseline came from files the agent may have rewritten, so no receipt is issued and that merge needs the waiver. `--ai-message` asks your configured model (`nexus worktree merge` takes the endpoint from your operator settings, never from a `.env` inside the worktree; a session's `
committed, capped at 20,000 characters and redacted, labelled as untrusted data; the reply is validated (at most 100
characters for the subject line, no control, C1 or bidi-override characters) and redacted; body lines shaped like commit trailers or release directives (`Release-As: ...`, `Co-Authored-By: ...`, `BREAKING CHANGE`) are dropped, and so is any ordinary line that happens to look like one. Any failure or a 30 second timeout falls
back with a note to the deterministic message, and an explicit `-m` always wins. No external command is run. Before history is rewritten the branch, including swept-in working-tree changes, is saved to
`refs/nexus-backup/<name>-<hash>`: one flat ref per branch, where `<name>` is the branch name with every character outside
`A-Za-z0-9._-` turned into `-` (at most 40 characters) and `<hash>` is the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-1 of the
branch name, so `foo` and `foo/bar` never collide (Git cannot hold both as refs). Find yours with
`git for-each-ref refs/nexus-backup`. Tracked Nexus state under `.nexus/` is left out of both the backup and the automatic commit, as `/commit` does. 63:6. **Container sandbox and argv isolation.** `--sandbox` confines execution using Linux Bubblewrap (`bwrap`) or Docker. The sandbox argv is constructed as a direct array without shell wrapping (REQ-SEC-109), preventing shell escaping flaws on complex workspace paths. In `--read-only` mode, `$HOME` is mounted as `--tmpfs $HOME`, completely masking SSH keys and dotfiles from commands (REQ-SEC-104); without bwrap, strict path confinement rejects paths outside the workspace. *Limit:* full container sandboxing requires `bwrap` or Docker on the host.
64:7. **Process group lifecycle and residual setsid escape risk.** The runner registers child process groups at spawn and terminates entire groups (`killpg`) on turn cancel, client crash, or process shutdown (REQ-AGT-109, REQ-SEC-106). Background services explicitly registered survive turn cancel but are cleaned on client exit. *Limit:* commands that explicitly invoke `setsid()` or create a new session ID escape the process group boundary unless Bubblewrap (`--sandbox`) or Docker isolation is enabled (`bwrap` uses `--die-with-parent` and PID namespaces to guarantee all descendants are swept). **Maturity:** Release notes for Nexus Code v1.1.3. This release carries the **entire v1.1.2 scope, unchanged**, under the version number v1.1.3.

## Why v1.1.3 and not v1.1.2

The command and flag claims check out against `cli/src`, `core/src` and `Makefile`. That covers the slash commands and their aliases, `--mode`, `--yes`, `--read-only`, `--sandbox`, `--worktree-branch`, the `NEXUS_CLOUD_MAX_*` variables, the `worktree switch -c`, `prune --dry-run` and `list --json` forms, `config.env`, `mcp.json`, Node 22+, Rust 2024 with MSRV 1.85 and toolchain 1.95.0, and the MIT/Apache split.

I did not find any code-review defects, only the false or unsupported claims below.

**Findings**
- **README.md:77, false claim.** The diagram lists `prlimit` as part of the sandbox. A repo-wide grep finds no `prlimit` use, and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` mentions only `bwrap` and Docker. Fix: change it to `Linux bwrap / Docker`.
- **README.md:78, unsupported claim.** `Worktrees[...feat/branch-name]` is a made-up path, and the actual location is `.nexus/worktrees/<branch>`. Fix: use `.nexus/worktrees/<branch>`.
- **README.md:74, noise.** The edge label "Fast IPC / CLI" is vague. The README's own text says the sidecar and the Rust core talk over NDJSON and a CLI. Fix: say that, or drop the label.
- **README.md:176, overclaim.** "zero risk to your checked-out files" is not something the repo guarantees. Fix: say "without touching your checked-out files".
- **docs/README.md:75, possible link problem.** `HISTORICAL.md` exists, but it is a record that the repo says is pinned by SHA-256. The entry describes it as "Early project milestones and architectural evolution", which does not match its content (the Issue #12 requirement and qualification records). Fix: describe it accurately, for example "Historical requirement and qualification records (Issue #12)".
- **README.md:274, overclaim.** "conflict-free merges" is false, because a worktree merge can conflict. Fix: say "receipt-gated merges".
- **README.md:45, marketing noise.** The "Most agentic coding tools operate either as..." sentence is a comparison the repo does not support. Fix: delete it or state it neutrally.
- **README.md:284, marketing noise.** "built with rigorous engineering standards" is empty filler. Fix: delete it.
- **README.md:60, unverified.** "syntax inspection" is listed as a capability of the Rust tools. I did not verify it in `core/src`. Fix: confirm it or remove it.
- **README.md:290, unverified.** The GitHub Discussions link has nothing in the repo to back it. Fix: confirm that Discussions is enabled, or remove the link.
- **README.md:161, duplicate sentence.** "Nexus Code works on the task without a terminal UI and exits..." restates the line above it. Fix: delete it.
- **Emoji debris.** There are emoji in the README section headings and Documentation Index bullets (README.md:168 and following sections, and around lines 267-276), and in every section heading of `docs/README.md` (🚀🏗️🌲🛠️🔐📜).
